name: Provisional Forces, Charleston Harbor (all troops under Beauregard)
location: Charleston harbour, Charleston County, South Carolina
units: South Carolina Army regulars (1st Artillery Battalion; 1st Regiment of Infantry); Regiment of Rifles; 1st Regiment S.C. Volunteers; 17th Regiment S.C. Militia (Cunningham); later Kershaw's, Hagood's and Rion's regiments; 2nd Artillery Battalion; Palmetto Guard; Marion Artillery; Vigilant Rifles; Charleston Light Dragoons; German Flying Artillery; C.S. Army recruits at Castle Pinckney
notes: STRENGTH IS AN ESTIMATE, NOT A RETURN: Walker, 4 Mar 1861, 'three thousand troops—the probable number now at Charleston'. Congress appropriated for 3,000 men plus 2,000 if needed (act of 11 Mar). Later figures: Pickens, 9 Apr: Morris Island raised to 2,100 men, ten companies (800 men) arriving that night and two regiments the next day, hoping for 'about six thousand men' on the harbour batteries and posts. Whiting, 11 Apr: 2,000 on Morris Island excluding artillery. No full return of the Charleston forces found. Side confederate for the command; almost all troops were S.C. State forces under Beauregard's orders (side state in the detachments). The only C.S. regular troops found are the Baltimore recruits at Castle Pinckney.

name: Castle Pinckney garrison: C.S. Army recruits (Capt. F. L. Childs)
location: Castle Pinckney, Charleston harbour, Charleston County, South Carolina
units: recruits for the C.S. Regular Army enlisted at Baltimore (Lts O'Brien and Robertson assigned)
notes: 64 recruits from Baltimore arrived on 23 Mar, were sent to Castle Pinckney and were to be enlisted on 25 Mar (Beauregard to Cooper). These are the only C.S. regular troops found at Charleston. On 9 Apr Childs, 'Commanding Castle Pinckney', was told to embark detachments of 25 men on each of three steamers nightly for Hartstene. Castle Pinckney itself was seized by State troops on 27 Dec 1860. Arm uncertain: the men were armed with muskets (Childs was an artillery officer).
sources: OR I-1 p.1; OR I-1 p.281; OR I-1 p.295

name: C.S. Navy guard steamers, Charleston (Commander H. J. Hartstene)
location: Charleston bar and harbour channels, South Carolina
units: Gordon (flag); Lady Davis (Lt Cmdg W. G. Dozier); General Clinch; also Charleston, Seabrook and Catawba on 9-10 Apr
notes: Orders of 5-6 Apr: prepare the Lady Davis with ten days' provisions; guard the approaches and prevent the reinforcement of Fort Sumter. No crew strengths found. Army detachments (25 men per steamer) were embarked nightly from 9 Apr.

name: Troops of the Confederate States near Pensacola (Bragg)
location: Pensacola Harbor (Warrington, Forts Barrancas and McRee), Escambia County, Florida
units: general staff; 1st Regiment Alabama, twelve months' volunteers; Georgia, twelve months' volunteers; Louisiana [volunteers] (row label OCR unclear)
notes: Field return of 31 Mar 1861 (extract): total 1,045 and 1,116, which the brief reads as present for duty and aggregate. Verified as sums: 839+109+97=1,045, and 885+113+101+17 (general staff)=1,116. Both OCR scans make the column headings illegible, so 'aggregate present' vs 'aggregate present and absent' cannot be told. The officer/men breakdown is OCR unclear: the 1st Alabama's first cells may read 46 and 793 (= 839) and the total row's 52 and 993 (= 1,045), not confirmed. Later strengths (no April return found): 7 Apr, 1,200 men expected that day from Mississippi and Georgia; 9 Apr, 1,600 arrived the day before and overnight; 14 Apr, 'Five thousand men here now, and two thousand more coming'. Bragg's enclosed strength statement of 14 Apr is 'Not found' by the compilers. 13 Apr: 'Every State is exceeding its quota.' 12 Apr: three Mississippi artillery companies and one Georgia company on the way. Requisition: 5,000 infantry. stores_days 90: the War Dept (14 Mar) notes 'three months' subsistence on hand for your present force' (from Bragg's dispatch of 12 Mar).

name: 1st Regiment Alabama Infantry, twelve months' volunteers
location: Pensacola Harbor (Warrington, Forts Barrancas and McRee), Escambia County, Florida
notes: Present for duty 839; aggregate 885 (31 Mar return). Gov. A. B. Moore, 19 Mar: Alabama troops at Pensacola feared transfer without electing their field officers; 'Nine companies will be there to-morrow' to form a regiment. Side confederate: listed on the C.S. field return.

name: General staff, troops near Pensacola
location: Pensacola Harbor (Warrington, Forts Barrancas and McRee), Escambia County, Florida
units: general staff (Col. John H. Forney, acting inspector-general; Robert C. Wood Jr., AAG; Capt. H. Oladowski, ordnance; others)
notes: 17 appears only in the aggregate column; no present-for-duty figure is printed for the staff, which is excluded from the 1,045 present-for-duty total.

name: Georgia twelve months' volunteers at Pensacola
location: Pensacola Harbor (Warrington, Forts Barrancas and McRee), Escambia County, Florida
notes: Present for duty 109; aggregate 113. Possibly Capt. G. W. Lee's company of 100 men (mostly artisans, from Atlanta), sent outside the Georgia quota on 19 Mar; this identification is not confirmed. Whether the 'Cavalry' column on the return applies to any row is OCR unclear.

name: Louisiana troops at Pensacola
location: Pensacola Harbor (Warrington, Forts Barrancas and McRee), Escambia County, Florida
units: Louisiana (row label OCR unclear in both scans)
notes: Present for duty 97; aggregate 101. The row label is garbled in both scans ('IOS PRIN VASES' / 'GHISIANA AOU AV CSS'); it is read as Louisiana following the brief and the row order. Possibly the advance of Coppens's Louisiana Zouave battalion (accepted 20 Mar, 400-500 men, 150 to be sent at once); not confirmed. Col. Gladden's Louisiana Volunteers were to send detachments to Pensacola after 8 Apr.

name: Regiment of Mounted Riflemen for C.S. service (being raised by H. E. McCulloch)
location: northwestern frontier, Texas
notes: Walker, 4 Mar: request to Maj. Ben McCulloch to raise the regiment, carried by C. L. Sayre, acting AAG, who was to muster it in. By 30 Mar Ben had transferred the order to his brother H. E. McCulloch, who was raising it; three of his five State companies on the NW frontier were to be mustered in. Walker, 15 Apr: supplies to be issued to companies of the Mounted Rifle Regiment as they are mustered.

name: 17th Regiment Infantry, South Carolina Militia (Col. John Cunningham)
location: Morris Island, Charleston County, South Carolina
notes: Cunningham signs as 'Colonel Seventeenth Reg. Inf., S.C.M.' in Dec 1860 (p.7). Beauregard to Col. Maxcy Gregg, 'Commanding Morris Island', 9 Apr: reinforcements to come, 'one or two regiments more besides the Seventeenth'. 418 is Whiting's figure of 11 Apr. 1st brigade (Simons) in GO 22.

name: 1st Artillery Battalion, South Carolina Army (Lt Col R. S. Ripley): Fort Moultrie and Sullivan's Island batteries
location: Fort Moultrie, Sullivan's Island, Charleston County, South Carolina
units: Companies A, B, D (Co. D 74 present, held for the floating battery). Batteries on 11-12 Apr: Fort Moultrie, 30 guns (Capt. W. R. Calhoun, assistant commandant; Channel and Sumter batteries under 1st Lts Thomas Wagner and Alfred Rhett); mortar battery No. 1 (2 x 10-in); enfilade battery, 4 guns (Capt. J. H. Hallonquist); Point battery, one 9-in Dahlgren, and floating battery, 4 guns (Capt. J. R. Hamilton, 1st Lt Yates); Mount Pleasant battery, 2 x 10-in mortars (Capt. Robert Martin, Infantry); Maffitt channel battery, 2 guns, and mortar battery No. 2, 2 x 10-in (Capt. Butler, Infantry); five-gun battery (Capt. Tupper, Vigilant Rifles)
notes: Ripley, 5 Mar: once Maj. Smith's battalion of the 1st S.C. Volunteers left, Fort Moultrie had 305 in total, including 63 Vigilant Rifles. That leaves 242 artillery, of whom Co. D had 74 total present, so 171 to man the guns (15 channel guns, 11 Sumter battery guns, 4 oblique guns, mortars). He gives the requirement as at least 190. CONFLICT: Ripley, 6 Mar, gives 'some 290 indifferent artillerymen (74 of the 290 held in readiness for special service)'. 242 (5 Mar) is used. Three companies of the 1st Infantry (Martin's, Butler's, Valentine's) were detached as artillerists under Ripley in April. Under Dunovant since 2 Jan 1861.

name: 1st Regiment of Infantry, South Carolina Army regulars (Col. Anderson): Sullivan's Island reserve
location: Sullivan's Island, Charleston County, South Carolina
units: Companies of Capt. Martin, Capt. Butler and Lt Valentine detached as artillerists under Ripley
notes: Dunovant, 21 Apr report: Colonel Anderson's 'regiment of the First Infantry' (also 'regiment of regulars') was held as a reserve on Sullivan's Island on 11-12 Apr. Strength not given.

name: 1st Regiment South Carolina Volunteers (Col. Maxcy Gregg)
location: Morris Island, Charleston County, South Carolina
units: 1st Regiment S.C. Volunteers (Maj. Smith's battalion moved from Fort Moultrie 5 Mar)
notes: Beauregard ordered the whole regiment to Morris Island with two short 12-pdrs and a light battery (report of 6 Mar). Maj. Smith's battalion embarked from Fort Moultrie on 5 Mar. 1,100 is Whiting's 11 Apr figure, unqualified (present for duty not stated). In GO 22 (15 Apr) it is in the 2nd brigade (Nelson).

name: 2nd Artillery Battalion (Lt Col W. G. De Saussure): Morris Island batteries
location: Morris Island, Charleston County, South Carolina
units: Cummings Point Iron battery (three 8-in columbiads) and Point battery (two 42-pdrs, a rifled 12-pdr, mortars), manned by the Palmetto Guard (Capt. G. B. Cuthbert) under Maj. P. F. Stevens of the Citadel Academy; Trapier mortar battery, Marion Artillery (Capt. J. G. King, S.C. Militia); Citadel cadets (Capt. Thomas, rifled cannon; Lt Armstrong); Lt Col Lamar's battery; Columbia Artillery (Capt. A. J. Green); Dahlgren channel battery (Lt Warley, C.S.N.)
notes: No strength given. Whiting, 11 Apr: De Saussure 'complains that he has not men enough to work his guns'. Before the new batteries, the Morris Island channel had seven 24-pdrs, two howitzers and two Dahlgrens mounted (Gwynn, 20 Mar), to which Captain Lee added two Dahlgrens, three columbiads, two sea-coast howitzers and two 24-pdrs. 1st brigade (Simons) in GO 22.

name: Floating battery (detachment of Company D, artillery battalion)
location: off the western end of Sullivan's Island, Charleston harbour, South Carolina
units: 4 guns (two 32-pdrs, two 42-pdrs per Ripley, with the Point battery); commanded by J. R. Hamilton with 1st Lts Yates and Harleston
notes: Company D was 74 total present on 5 Mar, 'in constant readiness for duty in the floating battery'. Only 'a portion of Company D' fought the battery on 12-13 Apr (Hamilton, 15 Apr), so 74 is the company, not the crew; 24 men of the Regiment of Rifles also went to it under fire. Already counted in the battalion block. CONFLICT on Hamilton's status: Ripley calls him 'Capt. J. R. Hamilton ... of the Artillery'; he signs 'Lieutenant, C.S. Navy' on 15 Apr (Callahan: resigned USN 15 Dec 1860).
sources: OR I-1 p.262; OR I-1 p.36; OR I-1 pp.39-40; OR I-1 p.317; Callahan p.242

name: Fort Johnson mortar batteries (Capt. George S. James)
location: Fort Johnson, James Island, Charleston County, South Carolina
units: Capt. George S. James's company; mortar battery on the beach and battery on the higher ground
notes: Fort Johnson was seized by State troops on 2 Jan 1861. Gwynn reported the beach mortar battery finished by 20 Mar. James 'had the honor of firing the first shell' on 12 Apr. Strength not given.
sources: OR I-1 p.1; OR I-1 p.31; OR I-1 p.34; OR I-1 p.271; OR I-1 p.277

name: Fort Palmetto, Stono Inlet (Capt. J. J. Pope Jr., light artillery)
location: Stono Inlet, Charleston County, South Carolina
notes: Pope reported on 7 Mar to Brig. Gen. Dunovant, and again on 12 Apr, that his force was small. No figure given.

name: Hagood's regiment, S.C. Volunteers
location: Morris Island, Charleston County, South Carolina
notes: Bonham, 12 Apr: 'the whole or a part of Colonel Hagood's regiment' was on Morris Island. 1st brigade (Simons) in GO 22.

name: Kershaw's regiment, S.C. Volunteers
location: Morris Island, Charleston County, South Carolina
notes: Whiting, 11 Apr: 'between 300 and 500'. Only a range is given, so strength is needs-source (range 300-500). Just arrived and 'helter-skelter' (Whiting). 2nd brigade (Nelson) in GO 22.

name: Forces on Morris Island
location: Morris Island, Charleston County, South Carolina
units: 1st Regiment S.C. Volunteers (Gregg); 17th Regiment S.C. Militia (Cunningham); Kershaw's regiment; Hagood's regiment (part or whole, by 12 Apr); battalion of Rion's regiment (by 15 Apr); 2nd Artillery Battalion (De Saussure) with Palmetto Guard, Marion Artillery and other companies
notes: Whiting, 11 Apr: 'Colonel Gregg has 1,100 men; Colonel Cunningham, 418; Colonel Kershaw, between 300 and 500—in all, 2,000, exclusive of artillery.' Pickens, 9 Apr: Morris Island forces raised to 2,100, with ten companies (800 men) due that night and two more regiments the next day. Neither is a formal return. Whiting, 11 Apr: 'There are no regulars here at all.'

name: Infantry recruits at Fort Moultrie (S.C. Army)
location: Fort Moultrie, Sullivan's Island, Charleston County, South Carolina
notes: Ripley, 6 Mar: '318 helpless infantry recruits, almost without arms, without clothing, and totally and entirely unfit to meet the enemy'. Not counted in his 5 Mar total. Presumably S.C. Army regular recruits; not checked against a return.

name: Regiment of Rifles (Col. J. Johnston Pettigrew): eastern Sullivan's Island
location: Sullivan's Island, Charleston County, South Carolina
units: Regiment of Rifles; attached 11 Apr: Charleston Light Dragoons (cavalry) and German Flying Artillery (field battery)
notes: 7 Mar: a detachment of 47 men was at Secessionville keeping communication open with Morris Island; Pettigrew addressed the S.C. Secretary of War (Jamison). 11 Apr: the regiment held the eastern third of Sullivan's Island with a picket on Long Island. Regimental strength not given.

name: Battalion of Col. Rion's regiment on Morris Island
location: Morris Island, Charleston County, South Carolina
notes: Named only in GO 22 (15 Apr), 2nd brigade (Nelson).

name: Vigilant Rifles (guard and gunners, five-gun battery, Sullivan's Island)
location: Sullivan's Island, Charleston County, South Carolina
notes: Ripley, 5 Mar: 63 Vigilant Rifles, all needed as guard for the five-gun battery. CONFLICT: Ripley, 6 Mar: '53 volunteers at the five-gun battery'. On 11-12 Apr Tupper commanded the five-gun battery.

name: Garrison of Fort Morgan (Alabama troops pending transfer)
location: Mobile Point, Baldwin County, Alabama
units: Alabama State troops; volunteer companies forming to fill the Fort Morgan contingent
notes: No strength return found. The Alabama A&IG (28 Mar) expected 'at least 400 of the troops at Fort Morgan' to agree to transfer to the C.S. On 6 Apr he expected the volunteer companies for the Fort Morgan contingent to be organised within the week, after which recruits enlisted before 28 Feb would be transferred. Requisition: 1,000. Side state because transfer was pending; post commander was Col. Hardee, C.S. Army.

name: Coast-guard detachments, 1st Battalion, 33rd Regiment S.C. Militia (Georgetown coast)
location: coast from North Island to Little River and the Santee entrance, Georgetown and Horry districts, South Carolina
units: Waccamaw Light Artillery (Capt. Daggett) 26 men and 2 officers; Watchesaw Riflemen (Capt. Ward) 20 and 2; Carolina Greys (Capt. Gillespie) 40 and 3; All Saints' Riflemen (Capt. Litchfield) 30 and 3; plus Capt. Johnson's company, 30 men and 2 officers, at the Santee redoubt
notes: Ordered out 13 Apr by the battalion's major (signature OCR unclear, 'W. C. White'?) in Col. Charles Allston Jr.'s absence: 146 men and 12 officers (158), plus 32 at the Santee River redoubt (190 in all). Reported to the S.C. Secretary of War, not to Beauregard, though within the command limits extended to Georgetown on 20 Mar.

name: Louisiana troops at Forts Jackson and St. Philip
location: Mississippi River below New Orleans, Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana
units: Louisiana State troops (artillery preferred for the forts)
notes: Number not given. Galt's orders (19 Mar) say the number serving at the forts was to be had from 'Brigadier-General Westmore' in New Orleans (name as printed), and that the troops for the forts 'should be of artillery'. Requisition: 700.
sources: OR IV-1 p.178; OR IV-1 p.135

name: Texas State mounted regiment (Col. John S. Ford): Rio Grande
location: lower Rio Grande, Texas
units: State regiment of mounted volunteers raised under an ordinance of the Texas Convention
notes: Gov. Clark, 4 Apr: asked the C.S. to accept 'the regiment of cavalry recently raised by Texas'. Walker, 10 Apr: would take this second regiment only as infantry for the Rio Grande. That this is Ford's regiment rests on H. E. McCulloch, 30 Mar ('the State regiment under Colonel Ford'). Strength not given.

name: Galveston batteries (S. Sherman, commandant)
location: Galveston, Galveston County, Texas
units: six 24-pdrs (two siege, four battery), two howitzers, two mortars; about 300 ball and shell from Brazos Santiago
notes: Sherman, 8 Mar, names guns but no men; he was setting up a beach battery with the help of Lt Stevens, late U.S. Engineers.

name: H. E. McCulloch's State companies, northwestern frontier
location: northwestern frontier from Red River to the Colorado, Texas
notes: H. E. McCulloch, 30 Mar: five companies actively defending the frontier under State authority, three to be mustered into C.S. service. Strength not given.

name: District of Columbia militia
location: Washington, District of Columbia
notes: About 600 on 18 April; up to about 2,000 volunteers under Stone at the inauguration (snippet). Scott asked for ten more District companies on 9 April (snippet). Same caveat as the regulars.

name: Fort Monroe garrison (Artillery School)
location: Old Point Comfort, Elizabeth City County, Virginia
units: Companies present in January 1861 per the detail order: C/1st, B/2nd, L/2nd, I/3rd, K/3rd, D/4th and one more company (OCR unclear) Artillery
notes: Strength needs-source. Company A, 1st Artillery left for Pensacola 24 Jan.

name: Key West garrison (Brannan)
location: Key West, Monroe County, Florida
notes: 'The scanty force (forty-four men) at my disposal.' Company letter needs-source.

name: Marine guard, Philadelphia Navy Yard
location: Philadelphia Navy Yard, Pennsylvania
units: Marine guard of the Philadelphia yard (Captain and Brevet Major Jacob Zeilin per NavyReg1861)
notes: No strength return inside the window was found. Lower bound: on 19 April Du Pont sent 'a guard of over fifty marines' to Norfolk in the Keystone State (ORN I-4 pp.283-284).

name: Marine Corps headquarters and barracks, Washington
location: Marine Barracks and Washington Navy Yard, District of Columbia
units: Marine Corps headquarters companies and the Washington yard guard
notes: No strength return inside the window was found. Lower bound from just after it: on 19 April Welles had 100 marines detailed from here for the Pawnee (ORN I-4 p.285), and a 34-man detachment from the Washington barracks reached Norfolk on 20 April (p.292). In January Toucey had sent 30 marines from here to Fort McHenry (p.263), and they returned when army troops relieved them.

name: Regulars in the Department of New Mexico
location: Santa Fe, Santa Fe County, New Mexico Territory (scattered posts)
notes: Loring's report of 23 March describes lost transport and stores after Texas seceded; no return found in OR I-1.

name: Regulars in the Department of the Pacific
location: San Francisco, San Francisco County, California (posts in California, Oregon and Washington Territory)
units: District of Oregon; troops in California and Nevada
notes: No return inside the window found. The June 1861 return (OR I-50) shows roughly two thousand present for duty, but the OCR table is unreadable: needs a clean copy.

name: Pickens expedition troops (steamship Atlantic)
location: at sea, New York to Santa Rosa Island, Florida
units: Barry's battery (Company A, 2nd Artillery); Hunt's Company M, 2nd Artillery; Duane's company of Engineer Sappers and Miners; Companies C and E, 3rd Infantry (Johns, Clitz); 20 Engineer carpenters
notes: Embarked New York 6 April, sailed 7 April. Brown's orders called for supplies for 1,000 men for six months (stores_days 180 refers to that order, for the reinforced post). One secondary chronology says 500 troops (research note): needs-source. Brooks's and Allen's companies, 2nd Artillery, and recruits followed in the Illinois (arrived about 17 April).
sources: OR I-1 pp.365-367, 372-373, 390; research note 2026-11-14-march-1861-facts.md q.7

name: Fort Pickens garrison
location: Fort Pickens, Santa Rosa Island, Escambia County, Florida
units: Company G, 1st Artillery (48); ordinary seamen from the Pensacola yard (31); 2 ordnance sergeants; 1 hospital steward
notes: Slemmer's count in January 1861: 82 'all told', 77 for duty. Count in March: needs-source. Brown later called Company G 'tainted' and attached newly joined men to Company A.

name: Home Squadron marines landed at Fort Pickens
location: Fort Pickens, Santa Rosa Island, Escambia County, Florida
units: Marine guards of the ships off Pensacola (Sabine, Brooklyn, St. Louis) under 1st Lt John C. Cash, USMC
notes: Landed the night of 12 April with Vogdes's company and kept in the fort at Vogdes's request (Adams, ORN I-4 p.115 and OR I-1 p.376). The count of 110 is from OR I-1 p.395. Earlier ship figures: the Brooklyn had 43 marines on 12 Feb (ORN I-4 p.82) and the St. Louis could land 20 on 19 Feb (p.84). These men are drawn from the ships' companies; whether the ORN I-1 crew figures include them is uncertain, so do not add the two counts together.

name: Company A, 1st Artillery (Vogdes), afloat
location: aboard USS Brooklyn, off Pensacola, Florida
units: Company A, 1st Artillery, filled to the maximum by privates attached from Companies C/1st, B and L/2nd, I and K/3rd, D/4th and L/4th(?) Artillery at Fort Monroe
notes: Embarked at Fort Monroe 23 Jan 1861 with three months' provisions (stores_days 90 counted from 23 Jan); off Pensacola from 6 Feb; transferred to the frigate Sabine before the March order arrived (Lincoln, message of 4 July 1861). Landed with 110 marines the night of 12 April. Exact strength needs-source.
sources: OR I-1 pp.353, 357, 395; Lincoln, message to Congress 4 July 1861 (msg_jul1861) p.5

name: US Revenue Cutter Harriet Lane
location: New York (by 30 March 1861); 4 March position needs-source
units: USRC Harriet Lane (side-wheel revenue steamer, about 600 tons; guns 5 or 2, see notes)
notes: A Treasury (Revenue Marine) vessel, not Navy; listed here only because she sailed with the Sumter expedition. Welles's orders of 30 March and 5 April put her temporarily under Navy orders (ORN I-4 pp.228, 236). Formal transfer to the Navy came on 17 Sept 1861 (ORN II-1 p.99). Captain John Faunce, U.S. Revenue Marine. On 31 March Welles also ordered 50 seamen sent to Norfolk in her (ORN I-4 p.273). She sailed from New York on 8 April, was first at the Charleston rendezvous on 11-12 April, and was back at New York on 18 April (pp.241, 249, 256). Guns conflict: the ORN I-4 list gives 619 tons and 5 guns; ORN II-1 p.99 gives a February 1861 battery of two 32-pdrs, 33 cwt (OCR reads '82-pdr'). ORN II-1 calls her the only steam vessel in the Revenue Cutter Service at the outbreak of war.

name: USS Anacostia (steam tender)
location: Washington Navy Yard, District of Columbia
units: USS Anacostia (screw steam tender, 217 tons, 1 gun)
notes: Not on the ORN I-1 list. NavyReg1861 p.97 lists her 'in service' at Washington. SecNav1861 counts 1 steam tender in commission with 1 gun; the other tender, John Hancock (3 guns), lay at San Francisco out of commission (SecNav1861 p.91). So the tender in commission was the Anacostia, with 1 gun (inference).

name: USS Brooklyn
location: Off Fort Pickens, Santa Rosa Island, Escambia County, Florida
notes: Strength is the 'Crew' column of the ORN I-1 list of vessels in commission on 4 March 1861. SecNav1861 counts complements 'exclusive of officers and marines', and the Home Squadron crews on that list sum to 1,981 against SecNav1861's 'about 2,000', so the column probably excludes officers and marines (inference). The OCR prints '25 1 259'. On 12 Feb Walker could land 93 armed men, not counting 43 marines or the engine-room hands (ORN I-4 p.82). Adams planned to land 140 from her (p.85). On 19 Feb she had 8 days' coal and 50 days' provisions (p.85). stores_days 21 is as of 16 March: provisions for crew, officers and troops on board, short of flour, butter, sugar, tea and beans (Paymaster Looker, p.96). She went to Key West for coal and provisions from about 22 to 31 March (pp.100-101, 104). Meigs gave her crew as 300 on 20 April (p.140).

name: USS Congress (flagship)
location: Off Montevideo, Uruguay
notes: Strength is the 'Crew' column of the ORN I-1 list of vessels in commission on 4 March 1861. SecNav1861 counts complements 'exclusive of officers and marines', and the Home Squadron crews on that list sum to 1,981 against SecNav1861's 'about 2,000', so the column probably excludes officers and marines (inference). Captain Louis M. Goldsborough as of Dec 1860 (SecNav1860 p.232); not re-checked for March. Ordered home by the letter of 9 April, which arrived on 15 June (ORN I-1 p.30).

name: USS Constellation (flagship)
location: Near the mouth of the Congo River, West Africa
notes: Strength is the 'Crew' column of the ORN I-1 list of vessels in commission on 4 March 1861. SecNav1861 counts complements 'exclusive of officers and marines', and the Home Squadron crews on that list sum to 1,981 against SecNav1861's 'about 2,000', so the column probably excludes officers and marines (inference). The tonnage is blank in the ORN I-1 OCR; 1,452 is from NavyReg1861 p.95 (columns scrambled, matched by row order). Captain J. S. Nicholas (SecNav1860 p.233; ORN I-1 p.24, April 1861). Inman's flagship; by April he had temporarily moved his flag to the Portsmouth (ORN I-1 p.24).
sources: ORN I-1 pp.xvi, 24; SecNav1860 p.233; NavyReg1861 p.95

name: USS Crusader
location: New York Navy Yard, Brooklyn, New York
notes: Strength is the 'Crew' column of the ORN I-1 list of vessels in commission on 4 March 1861. SecNav1861 counts complements 'exclusive of officers and marines', and the Home Squadron crews on that list sum to 1,981 against SecNav1861's 'about 2,000', so the column probably excludes officers and marines (inference). The OCR prints guns and crew as '87 70'. Read as 8 guns and 70 crew: NavyReg1861 (as read by Whittle, ORN II-1 p.451) gives 8 guns, and the squadron total of 187 needs 8. The crew figure is OCR unclear. The ORN I-4 list (covers all of 1861) gives 545 tons, 83 crew and 5 guns. Arrived New York 16 Feb under Lt J. N. Maffitt (ORN I-4 p.84). Lt T. A. M. Craven commanded by 11 March. Left New York 16 March carrying War Department dispatches for the Brooklyn, then stationed at Key West from about 25 March to protect public property (ORN I-4 pp.89-90, 95, 102-103). Meigs reckoned her crew at 100 on 20 April (ORN I-4 p.140).

name: USS Cumberland (flagship)
location: At sea, Vera Cruz to Hampton Roads
notes: Strength is the 'Crew' column of the ORN I-1 list of vessels in commission on 4 March 1861. SecNav1861 counts complements 'exclusive of officers and marines', and the Home Squadron crews on that list sum to 1,981 against SecNav1861's 'about 2,000', so the column probably excludes officers and marines (inference). Pendergrast hoisted his flag on 9 Feb (ORN I-4 p.86). The Powhatan towed her out of Sacrificios on 25 Feb. She reached Hampton Roads on 23 March, 27 days out (ORN I-4 p.266; SecNav1861 p.86; ORN II-1 p.69), needing repairs, water, stores and provisions (p.266). Moved to the Norfolk naval anchorage on 31 March (p.268). Welles kept her at Norfolk (SecNav1861 p.86; ORN I-4 p.278). The ORN I-4 list gives a crew of 288.
sources: ORN I-1 p.xv; ORN I-4 pp.xv, 86, 266-268, 278; ORN II-1 p.69; SecNav1861 p.86

name: USS Cyane
location: At sea, latitude 22° N, longitude 104° W, off western Mexico
notes: Strength is the 'Crew' column of the ORN I-1 list of vessels in commission on 4 March 1861. SecNav1861 counts complements 'exclusive of officers and marines', and the Home Squadron crews on that list sum to 1,981 against SecNav1861's 'about 2,000', so the column probably excludes officers and marines (inference). Commander Samuel Lockwood as of Dec 1860 (SecNav1860 p.234). Tonnage from NavyReg1861 p.95.
sources: ORN I-1 p.xvi; SecNav1860 p.234; NavyReg1861 p.95

units: Regular infantry, cavalry, artillery and Engineer Sappers and Miners (Duane's company left with the Pickens expedition on 6-7 April)
notes: About 600 regulars on 18 April, just after the window; 653 at the inauguration in an unidentified snippet. National Park Service figures via the research note; not checked against a public-domain primary. Marines at the navy yard (about 200 on 18 April) are Navy, not counted here.
sources: research note 2026-11-14-march-1861-facts.md q.15 (NPS, Civil War Defenses of Washington, ch.4); OR I-1 p.373
